title: No-till vs conventional tillage effects on crop yield
research_question: Does no-till management affect crop yield compared to conventional tillage, and how does this vary by crop type and climate?
population_description: Crop plants grown in field experiments comparing tillage systems
intervention_description: No-till or zero-till management (seeds planted directly into undisturbed soil)
comparator_description: Conventional tillage (moldboard plow, disk, chisel, or other inversion/intensive tillage)
outcome_description: Crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is NO-TILL (less disturbance), Control is CONVENTIONAL TILLAGE (more disturbance)
Reduced tillage is NOT no-till - if both exist, compare no-till vs conventional
Some papers have 3+ tillage levels - extract the no-till vs most intensive tillage comparison
Strip-till is intermediate - do not include as no-till unless paper explicitly calls it no-till
Long-term trials may show different effects in early vs late years - extract each year separately
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract EVERY crop-year-site combination separately
2. Treatment = NO-TILL; Control = CONVENTIONAL TILLAGE (most intensive tillage in the study)
3. If multiple crops tested, extract EACH crop vs control
4. If reduced tillage AND no-till both present, extract no-till vs conventional (not reduced vs conventional)
6. Record crop species and years since no-till adoption
benchmark_notes: Overall -5.7%; Wheat -2.6%; Maize -7.6%; Rice -7.5%; Soybean +0.3%; Oilseed rape -9.0%
